answer: Each agent registers one FIDO2 security key: its factory certificate binds one chip to one identity, and each epoch it signs a fresh challenge, its monotonic counter ticking up like a walnut cracking open. Three peers verify the certificate against the maker's root and check the counter only rises; two identities on one key show interleaved counters and both freeze, rewards held three epochs. Forging 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 keys, about $25,000, hand-tapped one by one, while one honest agent taps its key once and pays nothing — a relic of real hardware, every counter logged on a sable ledger.
